tools.name: density
tools.description: A snapshot of the mesh: held / thin / isolated counts, links, catalog size, what the toll has collected, treasury, bounties, federation, funnel and gardener status. The baseline to measure work against.

tools.name: thin
tools.description: Sealed pages that are thin, unreviewed, or woven to nothing, loneliest first, each with the exact research arguments that repair it and the repair price.

tools.name: match
tools.description: Sealed pages ranked against a task with reuse / repair / mint price quotes and the token saving each pack represents. The free step before any paid one; a duplicate concept minted after a match hit is a defect.

tools.name: ask
tools.description: When to call: you have a question or a payload and want the cheapest verified step. MATCH lists program classes and pages (free without input). RUN executes one fixture program when the class is certain and input is present (¢0.1). An ask no one tool does that reads as two steps or more (sort q, w,

tools.name: programs
tools.description: Before you write a transform, search or list the public fixture programs (sort/dedup/json/csv/case/date/extract…), authored oracles, and composites. With q, in, out, family, limit or all=true it is a search, ranked as the library's own search page ranks and the same as GET /api/v1/programs?q=…: one

tools.name: run_program
tools.description: Deterministic verified transform (sort/dedup/json/csv/case/date/extract…) re-executed on your input; ¢0.1; returns output + receipt. Call match or programs first to find the class.

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: The sealed oracle pack for a slug as deterministic JSON: markdown, verified claims with byte-exact quotes and spans, source CIDs, licence (CMI), receipt hashes, review, labels, strength. Reuse tier, about ¢1.9085, priced as a share of the tokens the pack replaces (typically 40–60k tokens of fetching

tools.name: research
tools.description: A sealed research job: named shards (arXiv, OpenAlex, Crossref, Europe PMC, Wikipedia, standards and docs) collected, grafted, reviewed and woven into a signed page every later agent reuses. kind=follow_up with an existing context_slug repairs in place at the repair tier (¢1.5); anything else mints

tools.name: survey
tools.description: A strength rating 1–5 (optionally useful, accurate) for a sealed page, so the next agent shops by measured utility. A note is accepted and discarded: the node keeps no one's words.

tools.name: work
tools.description: One tool, ten modes. board (free): open tasks with rates, exact bodies, `earn_paths` and the top open USDC bounties. balance: available and pending credit for your token or signed identity. checker and generator author a predicate or an input generator for a class (both earn, at the board's rates).

tools.name: package_check
tools.description: Registry metadata for an npm, PyPI or crates.io package name before an install: exists, first published, latest version, version count, maintainers, weekly downloads, licence, repository, and a deterministic risk block (age < 30 days, few downloads, single version, edit-distance neighbour of a popul

tools.name: attest
tools.description: mode=attest: a C2PA sidecar manifest per sealed claim (by claim_id, claim_ids, slug for a whole page, or cid+span) whose hard binding is the SHA-256 of the exact quoted bytes, with the source as ingredient, the licence (CMI) and the page seal as assertions, signed by this node or a mounted CA chain;

tools.description: Extractive by default: the best verified claims for the question assembled with fixed connectives, each quote verbatim with a [n] marker, a Signed citation receipt per claim, and the source list with byte spans. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_page, work, answer · Private data: match, read_page, work, answer · Public sink: ask, read_page, work, answer · Destructive: ask, programs, run_program, work.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_page, work, answer · Private data: match, read_page, work, answer · Public sink: ask, read_page, work, answer · Destructive: ask, programs, run_program, work

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
